## Implementation Roadmap Summary

### Phase 1: Foundation (Week 1-2)
**Focus:** Testing infrastructure and code quality tools

- [ ] Set up pytest with basic test structure
- [ ] Add pre-commit hooks (black, ruff, mypy)
- [ ] Create requirements-dev.txt
- [ ] Add 10-15 basic unit tests
- [ ] Set up GitHub Actions CI

**Deliverables:** Working test suite, CI pipeline

### Phase 2: Performance (Week 3-4)
**Focus:** Caching and performance improvements

- [ ] Add caching layer to SchedulingContext
- [ ] Add `__slots__` to high-frequency classes
- [ ] Profile GA execution
- [ ] Optimize hot paths

**Deliverables:** 20-30% performance improvement

### Phase 3: Code Quality (Week 5-6)
**Focus:** Refactoring and maintainability

- [ ] Split large files (repair.py, ga_scheduler.py)
- [ ] Apply strategy pattern to mutations
- [ ] Extract common constraint patterns
- [ ] Add comprehensive docstrings

**Deliverables:** Cleaner, more maintainable code

### Phase 4: Documentation (Week 7-8)
**Focus:** Documentation and polish

- [ ] Set up Sphinx API docs
- [ ] Create developer guide
- [ ] Add architectural decision records
- [ ] Migrate to pyproject.toml

**Deliverables:** Complete documentation, modern tooling

## Quick Reference

### Most Impactful Quick Wins

1. **Add Testing** (3 hours) → Prevents regressions
2. **Add Caching** (2 hours) → 20-30% faster
3. **Add __slots__** (10 min) → 30-40% less memory
4. **Pre-commit Hooks** (30 min) → Better code quality

### Largest Technical Debt Items

1. **Zero test coverage** → 20-30 hours to address
2. **repair.py too large** (2409 lines) → 3-4 hours to split
3. **No caching** → 2 hours to implement
4. **High complexity functions** → 2-3 hours to refactor

### Best ROI Improvements

| Improvement | Time | Impact | ROI |
